mechanism_narrative: A sustained low federal funds rate (FEDFUNDS) below 2.5% indicates accommodative monetary policy, reducing equity discount rates and boosting S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days through lower cost of capital for corporate investment.
failure_condition: The average 20-day forward return is negative during periods when FEDFUNDS is below 2.5% (the 25th percentile of historical values).

mechanism_narrative: A sharp increase in the federal funds rate (FEDFUNDS) above 4.0% within one month signals aggressive monetary tightening, increasing equity risk premiums and causing negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 20-day forward returns are positive in more than 55% of periods when FEDFUNDS rises above 4.0% in one month.

mechanism_narrative: Simultaneous growth in housing starts (HOUST) and decline in unemployment rate (UNRATE) signals robust economic expansion, increasing consumer spending and corporate earnings, leading to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: The joint signal (HOUST rising and UNRATE falling) produces positive 20-day returns in less than 45% of instances during expansionary periods.

mechanism_narrative: In late-cycle expansion regimes (characterized by housing starts above 2000 units), the S&P 500 experiences positive forward returns as investors anticipate peak economic activity and profit-taking, yielding positive 60-day returns.
failure_condition: The average 60-day forward return is negative during periods when HOUST exceeds 2000 and GDPC1 growth is above 2.0% annualized.

mechanism_narrative: A high unemployment rate (UNRATE) above 5.5% indicates weak labor market conditions, suppressing consumer spending and corporate earnings growth, causing negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: The average 5-day forward return is positive during periods when UNRATE exceeds 5.5% (the 75th percentile of historical values).

mechanism_narrative: A decline in unemployment rate (UNRATE) below 4.5% within one month signals a tight labor market, boosting consumer confidence and spending, leading to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 20-day forward returns are negative in more than 55% of periods when UNRATE falls below 4.5% in one month.

mechanism_narrative: Simultaneous decline in industrial production (INDPRO) and rise in consumer inflation (CPIAUCSL) signals stagflation, increasing equity risk premiums and causing negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: The joint signal (INDPRO falling and CPIAUCSL rising) produces negative 20-day returns in less than 45% of instances during stagflationary periods.

mechanism_narrative: In supply shock recovery regimes (evidenced by industrial production (INDPRO) above 115), the S&P 500 rises as economic activity normalizes and supply chains stabilize, yielding positive 60-day forward returns.
failure_condition: The average 60-day forward return is negative during periods when INDPRO exceeds 115 (the 75th percentile of historical values).
